question:
A 71-year-old male with a history of hypertension and stable coronary artery disease comes for a
routine follow-up visit. His daughter expresses concern that he has been isolating himself at home and
not answering phone calls. She also notes that during a recent family reunion, he appeared sad and
withdrawn, despite having anticipated the event for months. The patient states he does not recall his
daughter calling and denies intentionally ignoring calls. He explains that he prefers staying home to
avoid crowded environments and mentions difficulty keeping up with conversations at the reunion,

especially with family members wearing face masks. During the interview, he struggles to understand
questions, frequently looks to his daughter with a confused and embarrassed expression, and asks for
questions to be repeated. His Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ)-2 score is 0, and his Mini-Cog
assessment score is 4 (2/2 on the clock-drawing test and 2/3 on word recall). Physical and neurologic
examinations are unremarkable. What is the most appropriate next step in the management of this
patient? Answer Choices: (A) Order brain MRI with contrast (B) Schedule formal neuropsychological
testing (C) Initiate cognitive behavioral therapy (D) Refer for audiology evaluation now (E) Order thyroid
function tests (F) Perform otoscopic evaluation (G) Administer the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (H)
Recommend social work consultation (I) Start donepezil therapy (J) Schedule follow-up in 3 months
 A. Refer for audiology evaluation now
B. Start donepezil therapy
C. Perform otoscopic evaluation
D. Order thyroid function tests
E. Schedule formal neuropsychological testing
F. Recommend social work consultation
G. Administer the Montreal Cognitive Assessment
H. Order brain MRI with contrast
I. Initiate cognitive behavioral therapy
J. Schedule follow-up in 3 months
